findings.title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy values for old flexbox syntaxes
findings.body: The mixin writes the same $alignment into -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align. Those legacy properties use different keywords: `center` is valid, but `baseline` is valid in both while `flex-start` and `flex-end` must be `start` and `end`. Callers passing `flex-start` or `flex-end` get invalid declarations on those engines. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property. Prefer a keyword translation or drop the nonexistent prefix.

findings.title: order mixin uses the same value for box-ordinal-group
findings.body: The `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties are 1-based and are not equivalent to the modern `order`, which defaults to 0. In `header.scss`, `.panel` uses order(3) while the unordered siblings have the default order, so the old-box fallback yields different ordering than modern flexbox.

findings.title: Removing .title float and making .contents flex may break header layout
findings.body: The `.title` float rule was removed and `.contents` became a flex container, yet `.panel` relies on `margin-left: auto`. The `.contents` children (logo, extra-info-wrapper, panel) now depend on order values. Only `.extra-info-wrapper` (order 2) and `.panel` (order 3) are given an order, and the title stays at the default 0, which works only if the title is the first child. The `.icons`, `.login-button` floats inside the flex `.panel` are unchanged, so the panel may collapse. Also, other stylesheets, such as mobile or desktop ones, that still set floats on these elements are not updated.

findings.title: Flex on .small-action has float and clear on flex items and container
findings.body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container but children still use `float` (`.topic-avatar`, `.avatar`, `button`). Floats are ignored on flex items, so the `button` float:right no longer pushes the button to the right. The fixed `padding: 0 1.5%` replaces the earlier 4em left offset and the removal of the margins and paddings changes the vertical spacing of small-action posts, which is a visible regression unrelated to the header title.
